cards.text: Paul, the apostle, is writing to the believers in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7). He's been talking about his own people, Israel, and how not all of them welcomed the good news (Romans 10:16). So now he asks it straight out: 'I ask then, did God reject His people?'

cards.question: True or false: Paul answers that yes, God has rejected His people Israel.
Paul says CERTAINLY NOT, then points to himself as an Israelite and a descendant of Abraham. Which tribe is Paul from?

cards.text: If God threw out Israel, He'd have to throw out the guy WRITING THE LETTER! Paul says God did not reject His people, whom He foreknew, and then he brings up Elijah, a prophet of Israel, on one of his roughest days.

cards.question: Paul reminds them what the Scripture says about Elijah: he appealed to God ___ Israel.

cards.text: And Elijah does NOT hold back. He says, 'Lord, they have killed Your prophets and torn down Your altars.'

cards.question: Elijah tells God His prophets are killed and His altars are torn down. Then he tells God who's left. What does Elijah say?

answers.text: He is the only one left

cards.question: True or false: Elijah tells God that the people are seeking his life as well.

cards.text: Elijah's sure he's the last one left. I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer thinking that, friend, so Paul's next question gets me right in the apron: 'And what was the divine reply to him?'

cards.question: God replies to Elijah, 'I have reserved for Myself seven thousand men…' What makes those seven thousand stand out?

answers.text: They have not bowed the knee to Baal
They have hidden all of God's prophets
They have rebuilt all of God's altars

cards.question: True or false: God's reply means Elijah was not the only one left who hadn't bowed the knee to Baal.

cards.text: Elijah's story wasn't just a trip down memory lane, friend. Paul says God is doing it the same way right now, in his own day.

cards.question: Like the seven thousand in Elijah's day, Paul says there is something at the present time. What is it?
Paul says this remnant is chosen by ___.
True or false: Paul says the remnant is chosen partly by grace and partly by works.

cards.text: Paul says if it's by grace, it's no longer by works, or grace would no longer be grace. Grace you earn isn't a gift, friend, that's a PAYCHECK!
What then? Paul says what Israel was seeking, it failed to obtain.

cards.question: True or false: Israel failed to obtain what it was seeking, but Paul says the elect did obtain it.
And the rest of Israel? Paul says the others were ___.

cards.text: Paul backs that up with Scripture: 'God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that could not see, and ears that could not hear, to this very day.'

cards.question: Paul quotes Scripture about eyes that could not see and ears that could not hear. Which group in Israel is he describing?

answers.text: The seven thousand in Elijah's day

cards.text: Then Paul brings in David, Israel's king, who says, 'May their table become a snare and a trap, a stumbling block and a retribution to them.'
David goes on, 'May their eyes be darkened so they cannot see, and their backs be bent forever.' Heavy words, friend.

cards.question: True or false: David's line about eyes being darkened so they cannot see paints the same picture as the Scripture Paul quoted just before, about eyes that could not see.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin says he spent YEARS in the junk drawer thinking he was the last one left. His backstory says the opposite. He wasn't the only one stuck in there, and the drawer friends were 'all in it together.' The joke changes his story to fit the comparison.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: 'On one of his roughest days' states a Bible fact about Elijah's situation (1 Kings 19) that is not in this passage, with no reference. It also steers the baker toward 'against' on the next card.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The true or false card about 'partly by grace and partly by works' (11:6) comes before any story card tells 11:6. Nothing earlier lets the baker reason it out. Card 5 then explains 11:6 after the question, so the setup and the question are in the wrong order.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'rewarded' isn't believable. The card right before says Israel failed to obtain what it was seeking, so being rewarded doesn't fit. The card becomes a choice between two answers.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Story cards 6, 9 and 11 are bare paraphrase or quotation with no Papa Dorin voice, and card 12 adds only 'Heavy words, friend.' Stop 2 has one joke (card 5).

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The passage ends mid-argument on David's harsh words ('their backs be bent forever'). Paul's next verse (11:11) answers this right away: 'did they stumble so as to fall? Certainly not!' The passage has no story group, so the 'story isn't over' rule doesn't apply, and the baker leaves on the hardening with no sign the teaching continues.
findings.question: When a Letters passage has no story group but its argument clearly continues into the next verse, should the last story card get a line saying the teaching isn't done?
